column4: Accelerates development and industrialisation of agentic AI use cases across group control. Claude Code stands up, iterates and scales agentic systems requiring sophisticated scaffolding — security, scalability and production requirements built in from onset. Embeds relevant context (policy/procedure docs) to generate compliant systems. Enables adaptability as agentic AI frameworks evolve rapidly.
column5:
- Faster time-to-value: rapid PoC identification and target benefits control
- Accelerated delivery of production-ready code
- Flexibility to remain at the cutting edge
- Operational efficiency: process automation frees analyst capacity for higher-value work
column8: Directly addresses the team's core mandate. Agentic AI is the highest-growth area and Claude Code removes the two biggest bottlenecks: development speed and production readiness. Proven via TM and Comms Surveillance pilots already delivering results.

column4: Accelerates development and industrialisation of ML models for fraud and financial crime. Reduces time to deploy high-impact models. Enables broader experimentation across methodology, data sources and feature engineering. Supports end-to-end, production-ready ML pipelines with reproducibility, auditability, security and scalability built in. Ensures consistency of technical artefacts with non-technical MRM artefacts (model docs, monitoring, implementation testing).
column5:
- Direct financial impact: faster deployment of fraud models accelerates loss prevention
- Improved model performance from small incremental uplifts
- Increased innovation throughput: more PoCs without headcount
- Exploration of deprioritised opportunities
- Reduced rework and stronger governance outcomes
column8: ML model development is the team's bread and butter. Even small performance uplifts yield material financial benefit given the fraud detection scale. Governance alignment through consistent artefacts is a strong differentiator. High-leverage, well-justified.

column3: Innovation and Solution for TM Lifecycle
column4: Covers end-to-end TM lifecycle activities. Uses GenAI and ML to design targeted solutions for: reducing false positive alert noise, improving typology and risk coverage, enhancing process efficiency and automation. Enables faster testing, time-to-market deployment, simplified processes and standardised pipelines of development.
column5:
- Simplified process: more team members can work on projects
- Improved consistency, standardised framework
- Validation, reviews and audit readiness
column8: Solid focus area that addresses a real pain point (FP noise in TM). Benefits are clear but description is somewhat broad — would benefit from tighter scoping around specific TM lifecycle stages. Owner and licence ownership not yet confirmed.

column4: Claude generates first-pass DAG scaffolds (task groups, dependencies, retries, SLAs) aligned to GCDA's Airflow configuration internally. Codifies GCDA templates for DAG-to-DAG triggers and modular composition. Reduces orchestration toil so engineers focus on correctness and operational constraints. Outputs treated as draft code with merges requiring human peer review, test evidence and adherence to standard best practices.
column5:
- Faster onboarding of new workflows via templates
- Improved reliability via standard patterns
- Higher auditability (explicit DAG structure over ad-hoc scripts)
column8: Airflow is the default orchestrator across on-prem ElasticDP pods — standardisation impact is broad. Proven: Claude can write high-quality Python code. Leverage is high given every pipeline benefits. Solid but somewhat infrastructure-focused rather than directly crime-prevention linked.

column3: Foundation Package for Shared Portfolio Functions (FunctionForge)
column4: FunctionForge is the shared execution layer across GCQA model portfolios. Claude codifies common logic safely — generating first-pass implementations for shared preprocessing, filtering, training, calibration helpers and validation utilities. Refactors near-duplicate logic from multiple model codebases into single, parameterised implementations. All Claude-generated code treated as draft, reviewed, tested via standard CI and approved through existing peer process.
column5:
- Reduced duplication of logic across ML pipeline
- Faster onboarding of new models onto standard patterns
- Lower defect and regression risk via single, well-tested implementations
- Clear architectural separation between shared and bespoke code
column8: One of the highest-leverage uses: FunctionForge code executes across multiple model portfolios, so quality and reuse improvements compound. Removes repeated engineering effort and systemic risk simultaneously. Well-scoped and production-safe framing.

column4: Claude provides test scaffolding at scale by generating first-pass pytest suites and coverage harnesses for repetitive components (config validation, pipeline utilities). Helps draft and standardise CI steps for testing, linting and release in the central GitLab workspace. Enforces 'no merge without tests/coverage evidence'. Reduces engineering toil, leaving more time for parameterisation and meaningful design.
column5:
- Comprehensive test suites increasing code robustness in production
- Higher reproducibility and maintainability
- Lower support burden via standard patterns
column8: Standard CI + tests reduce defect leakage and improve delivery throughput across every repo. Mitigates fragmentation risk. Proven: Claude writes high-quality Python with right prompting. Good value but derivative of FunctionForge — consider whether it should be a sub-item.

column4: Claude accelerates integration work and produces consistent experiment templates, improving reproducibility. Generates scaffolding for experiment tracking and promotes consistent metadata capture. Experiments remain human-owned.
column5:
- Faster iteration with less rework
- Improved reproducibility and governance
- Better cross-team comparability
column8: Central experiment tracking reduces rework and supports auditability. Standardised templates accelerate onboarding. Value is solid but narrower than FunctionForge or CI pipeline use cases. Included in delivery modernisation theme.

column4: Claude drafts conversion utilities and regression/parity test scaffolds, reducing manual effort significantly for format migration, particularly for complex model pipelines. Focuses on equivalence-checking artefacts (tests, validation scripts) so conversion doesn't introduce behavioural drift.
column5:
- Reduced deployment friction
- Improved portability/standardisation
- Lower long-term maintenance cost
column8: Format modernisation is high-leverage: once ONNX is standard, automation, portability, reliability and pace improve across all deployments. Proven: Claude writes high-quality Python. Benefit is clear, though timing depends on ONNX migration programme pace.

column4: Claude accelerates and enhances generation of repeatable validation logic for DQ. Can produce dashboard scaffolding for DQR to increase observability. DQ rules remain SME-approved — Claude used as a boilerplate, not to autonomously define business logic thresholds.
column5:
- Earlier detection of data issues
- Reduced defects and rework
- Clear, auditable DQ reporting
column8: DQ is a cross-cutting concern upstream of every pipeline; reusable and enhanced DQ frameworks provide compounding returns for DE and ease of operation downstream. Smart governance framing (SME-approved rules) makes this safe and credible.

column4: Claude Code helps understand codebases in a maintain-and-divest state where the team lacks C# skill expertise. Provides an abstraction layer between the lightly-documented codebase and senior engineers. Intent is to allow senior engineers to understand the legacy codebase rather than build or develop something new.
column5:
- Reduced risk from poorly documented legacy systems and tech debt
- Allows team to avoid hiring specialist contractors
column8: Legitimate use: avoiding niche skill investment for a divest-state tool is sensible. However, this is a maintenance/risk-mitigation play rather than value creation. Value ceiling is low and the problem should ideally be solved by decommissioning, not perpetuating.

column4: Claude Code assists as the team replatforms its transform layer from Hypercube to EDP. Builds the conformance layer, creates a DQ test suite via dbt-test models, translates legacy datasets, discovers breaking changes, creates data products documentation, and enables Data Products enablement. Estimated 30–50% reduction in manual engineering effort.
column5:
- Reduce manual engineering effort during development of new DW assets on EDP
- Reduce risk of data errors during replatforming
- Rapid, templated creation of new data quality layer
- Automated documentation
column8: High-value, well-scoped use case with a quantified effort-saving estimate (30–50%). Claude Code is genuinely well-suited to templated exercises like building dbt models and conformed view definitions. Data warehouse replatforming is engineering-heavy and the benefits are concrete.

column3: Model Development (Retail, Credit, BB, PB, Mules)
column4: Claude speeds up early stages of model development by drafting initial versions of feature engineering code, training pipelines, evaluation scripts and standard project structure. Reflects patterns already used across Fraud and Mules, allowing engineers to start from something concrete rather than from scratch. All modelling choices, assumptions and decisions remain with engineers and SMEs.
column5:
- Faster delivery of new and redeveloped models
- More consistent implementation across portfolios
- Fewer avoidable differences driven by individual coding style
- Easier comparison and review between models
column8: Mirrors the ML Model Development use case for the Fraud & Mules portfolio specifically. Benefits are direct, measurable and proven. Consistency across portfolios (Retail, Credit, BB, PB) maximises leverage. Well-governed framing with human decision ownership.

column4: Claude supports refresh work by drafting updated pipelines, refreshed sampling logic and comparison code to assess changes against previous behaviour. Using a consistent refresh approach lowers the risk of refresh-specific defects being introduced under delivery pressure, particularly where the intent is to maintain behaviour rather than materially change it.
column5:
- More predictable refresh outcomes
- Reduced likelihood of manual errors under time pressure
- Clearer understanding of what has and hasn't changed
- Less rework following refresh delivery
column8: Refreshes are frequent, deadline-driven and repetitive — exactly the use case where standardisation reduces risk. Consistent templating reduces inadvertent drift. Clear, well-justified with low governance risk.

column4: Claude quickly drafts analysis code for investigations such as cohort breakdowns, trend analysis, drift checks and alert reviews. Standardises how common investigative questions are approached across cases. More consistent analysis patterns reduce the risk of different conclusions being reached simply due to differences in how analysis is set up.
column5:
- Faster and more consistent investigations
- Reduced variability in analytical approach
- Easier comparison across cases and time periods
- Better reuse of established investigative patterns
column8: Investigations are urgent and repeated across teams. Standardising the analysis setup improves reliability while reducing time to insight. Well-justified and practical. Claude consistently produces sensible analytical scaffolding when guided by experienced fraud analysts.

column4: Claude helps teams stand up PoCs quickly by drafting experimental pipelines and feature exploration code in clearly non-production environments. Encourages early testing and early failure where appropriate. Being able to discard weak ideas quickly reduces the risk of poorly-understood approaches progressing too far into delivery.
column5:
- Quicker signal on whether ideas are viable
- Reduced risk of over-investing in weak approaches
- Clear separation between experimentation and production
- Better-informed prioritisation decisions
column8: Rapid, low-cost experimentation improves decision-making on what should and should not progress. Claude is effective for early-stage exploration where speed matters most. Proven in adjacent areas. Strong value-for-licence proposition.

column4: Detect and prevent erroneous payments by identifying incorrect, duplicate or anomalous payments where the bank may lose control of funds — including payments with incorrect/outdated SSIs, duplicate payments triggered days apart, and unusual patterns caused by human error, process failures or control gaps. Claude Code generates and standardises complex detection logic for SSI validation, duplicate payment detection and anomaly detection across large transaction volumes. Maintains consistent pipeline structure, testing scaffolds and documentation.
column5:
- More maintainable and auditable analytics pipelines aligned with governance expectations
- Scalable foundation extendable to new payment types, typologies and regions
- Reduces operational risk by standardising analytical implementations
- Improves reviewability of EP detection logic through consistent, well-documented code
- Increases analyst productivity by automating repetitive development tasks
column8: Well-scoped, financially material use case. EP detection is technically complex but structurally repeatable — exactly the profile where Claude Code adds most value. Governance and auditability framing is strong. Quantified financial and reputational impact makes this easy to justify.

column4: Introduce an automated, intelligent pre-QC layer inside the TM workflow performing 100% first-level quality checks before cases go to QC/QA. Uses NLP/GenAI to compare analyst narrative against existing QC error codes (missed transactions, incomplete SoF/SoW, inadequate rationale for international activity, insufficient risk indicator documentation) and provides real-time structured prompts to highlight potential gaps — without generating conclusions or replacing analyst judgement. Phased rollout starting with high-impact QC error codes.
column5:
- Faster build and iteration of the pre-QC NLP/GenAI layer
- More production-ready, standardised implementation (security/scalability patterns baked in early)
- Improved auditability and governance alignment via consistent engineering artefacts
- Quicker adaptation to changing QC codes/policy
- Context-embedded development: policy/procedure context embedded directly into build artefacts
column8: High-leverage use case: TM QC is constrained by sampling capacity while case volumes are large. Scale + repeatable build + governance alignment makes this a strong fit for Claude Code licences. Already formally discussed as a priority domain (TC01) with operations. Proven adjacent automation (KYC QC) validates approach.

column4: Automate and accelerate mapping of internal controls to Legal, Regulatory and Rules-based (LRR) obligations published by OLO. Identifies the most relevant obligation matches for each control across large obligation packs, reducing manual line-by-line review effort while improving consistency, traceability and scalability for CCO mapping teams. Claude Code enables this as a production-ready, auditable software pipeline — scaffolding pipelines, standardising logic, maintaining traceability, agent orchestration, scoring and ranking outputs, and version-controlled documentation.
column5:
- Claude Code accelerates standing up and iterating an agentic mapping pipeline
- Helps architect more robust, production-ready code with security/scalability from outset
- Context-embedded development: embeds policy/obligation context directly
- Rapid re-runs and adaptability as OLO obligation packs change
- Reduced engineering toil: automates repetitive scaffolding
- Decisioning rather than boilerplate build work for SMEs
column8: Technically complex, highly repeatable, and currently consumes 20–25 FTEs for BUK alone. Claude Code is appropriate here not as a standalone AI but as the engineering accelerant. Partially proven through existing comparable analytics applications. Regulatory importance and scale make this one of the strongest use cases in the register.

column3: QA Automation – Debit Card Reissue Calls (CCO)
column4: Automate QA for debit card reissue customer calls by moving from manual sample-based review (50–100 calls per month) to full-population, data-driven QA control. Analyses AWS Connect call transcripts, FullServe agent actions and downstream customer outcomes to automatically classify customer requests, reconcile agent actions against standard procedures, and verify whether the intended outcome was achieved. Identifies repeat calls, delays, unmet outcomes and unauthorised actions across high-volume, high-risk call flows. Claude Code accelerates build by generating and refactoring core components: transcript ingestion, request classification, reconciliation rules, agent orchestration, scoring and QA output. Enables testable, reviewable pipelines and creation of test harnesses, validation checks and consistent documentation.
column5:
- Capacity release: process automation frees SME/analyst time for higher-value review and remediation
- Faster time-to-value: rapid prototyping to scale the QA pipeline quickly
- Production-ready delivery: helps architect robust code with security/scalability from day one
- Governance alignment: embeds policy/procedure context so outputs better meet control and compliance requirements
column8: Full-population QA from a manual sample is a significant operational improvement. The use case is specific, well-scoped and the engineering pattern (transcript ingestion → classification → reconciliation → output) is repeatable. Proven: automated call analytics, transcript classification and outcome reconciliation are well-established in QA and customer operations.

column4: Automate and accelerate CAAR (Customer Account Activity Review) workflow by: (1) extracting and structuring inputs from the NoB/SoF (NobSof) transaction report and related sources, (2) generating consistent 'Nature of Business + expected payment flows' narrative including industry inference from nature-of-business text, and (3) producing repeatable payment-review and account-turnover summaries (incl. flags for sanctioned/restricted country exposure and unusual patterns) to support faster, higher-quality CAAR completion with human sign-off. Claude Code builds and maintains end-to-end automation pipeline (data ingestion → rules/metrics → anomaly checks → narrative generation): drafting and refactoring multi-file Python code for parsing NobSof/transaction extracts, standardising feature calculations, packaging the workflow for reuse, rapidly scaffolding production-ready components, helping embed internal workflow/context into the codebase as prompts/templates, and reducing iteration time when rules evolve (sanctioned country logic, cash verification steps, edge-case handling in transaction reports) without compromising SDLC controls.
column5:
- Accelerates development and iteration by generating production-aligned code scaffolds, reducing setup time and enabling faster progression from analysis to deployable solutions
- Improves consistency and quality through standardised patterns, reducing variation caused by individual coding styles and lowering rework during reviews and refreshes
- Strengthens governance and audit readiness by supporting reproducible, well-documented code and aligned artefacts meeting model risk, validation and control expectations
- Scales analytical productivity without additional headcount by automating repetitive engineering tasks
column8: Engineering-heavy (data wrangling, repeatable calculations, standardised narratives, governance artefacts). Claude Code provides leverage where most time is typically spent: building boilerplate, tests and maintainable pipeline structure. Faster delivery, less rework, more reliable outputs for an operationally critical CAAR workflow — while keeping final judgement with CSH/RDs. Proven in adjacent comparable areas.

column4: Identify potential insider-threat risk by analysing employee behavioural patterns across multiple data sources (access logs, check-in/check-out data, camera signals, system usage) to surface anomalous or high-risk behaviour for early intervention. Claude Code accelerates development of complex, multi-source analytics by generating consistent, production-aligned scaffolding for data ingestion, feature engineering, behavioural metrics and risk-scoring pipelines. Enables rapid iteration on hypotheses while embedding existing coding standards, governance requirements and documentation patterns from the outset.
column5:
- Faster development and iteration of behavioural risk features and analytics
- Improved consistency and comparability across models and metrics
- Reduced implementation risk through standardised, well-documented code patterns
- Better analyst focus on risk interpretation rather than pipeline engineering
column8: Insider threat detection requires frequent experimentation, refinement of behavioural signals and careful governance — all areas where Claude Code reduces engineering toil. Value is real but the use case is earlier-stage and more experimental than others. Similar Claude Code applications in fraud, financial crime and surveillance analytics have shown clear value in accelerating development.

column3: BUK Application Models Development and Monitoring
column4: Claude accelerates consistent feature-engineering scaffolding across portfolios, embedding policy definitions and MRD logic directly into code templates and reducing manual re-implementation errors when porting logic between products (credit cards, loans, current accounts). Claude also assists by accelerating experimentation through the creation of feature-engineering pipelines in clearly delineated non-production environments. Key benefits include accelerated delivery of production-ready code, reduced re-work by embedding security, scalability and governance early, feature experimentation across portfolios, avoiding costly redesigns when engaging technology teams for platform upgrades.
column5:
- Generate validation checks (edge cases, indeterminate frauds, missing investigations)
- Speed up retros logic prototyping for PoCs and recalibrations
- Reducing re-work when models move from PoC to production and from legacy to new decisioning platform
column8: Solid application of Claude Code to a complex multi-portfolio, multi-product problem. Benefits are clear and the consistency argument across Retail, Credit, BB and PB is compelling. Slightly overlaps with use case #12 (Fraud & Mules Model Development) — consider whether to consolidate or differentiate by platform context.

column4: Claude Code helps with EDP migration by enabling a proper like-for-like comparison of vendor tools to ensure the most effective option is chosen. Speeds up the shift from SAS to a Python-based framework, simplifies existing pipelines and reduces manual effort. Enhanced Ways of Working: supports setup of improved analytical frameworks, enabling better-quality analytics and improving analyst turnaround time and efficiency. Automation reduces migration effort and overall SAS exit costs. Productivity gains from quicker code conversion and fewer manual checks. Value extends beyond SAS exit — Claude can support broader analytics, QA and documentation tasks.
column5:
- Benefit case: reduction in migration effort/cost
- Higher-quality, standardised target-state pipelines
column8: SAS → Python migration is a real, time-bound engineering challenge. Claude Code's value for code conversion and pipeline simplification is well-proven. Benefits are tangible. The use case is somewhat transitional in nature (it terminates when migration is complete) but the value during the migration window is clear and the analytics quality improvement is durable.

column4: Many existing financial-crime, onboarding and control processes run on Teradata and SAS with complex, undocumented business logic. To modernise and support Databricks adoption, Claude Code reverse-engineers these legacy scripts and rebuilds them as scalable data pipelines. Proposed solution: reverse-engineer Teradata and SAS scripts to extract conceptual mappings (high-level flow of entities and business rules), logical mappings (detailed field-level transformations) and physical mappings (platform-specific technical mappings). Once validated, auto-generate Python/SQL code for Databricks (Delta pipelines, notebooks or workflows). Claude also enriches records for data quality, metadata tagging, category tagging (PII, high-risk, regulated) and standardisation for downstream pipelines.
column5:
- Preserves institutional knowledge embedded in legacy scripts
- Accelerates migration to Databricks
- Ensures traceability for regulatory/FC/CO use cases
- Reduces manual effort in data modelling and engineering
- Improves data quality and reduces interpretation errors
- Supports Data Design, DPIA, PII/CI/CS controlled and documentation production
column8: Addresses a genuine and significant engineering bottleneck across financial crime, onboarding and control processes. The combination of legacy script comprehension, structured extraction and code generation is exactly where Claude Code adds most value. Governance and traceability requirements make automated documentation and metadata tagging especially valuable. High-effort, high-reward.

column4: Claude supports end-to-end data modelling by generating complete conceptual and logical models using inputs such as business requirements, Jira stories, SME discussions, process flowsand legacy schemas. It identifies entities, relationships, attributes, cardinality, keys and semantic gaps, ensuring alignment with BCDM and enterprise modelling guidelines. It also performs attribute rationalisation across SDS, EDP and legacy sources to remove duplicates, standardise naming and converge similar fields. Claude validates EDP readiness by assessing metadata completeness, domain alignment, CDE/EDE mapping, partitioning strategy, granularity and lineage availability. It detects PII and sensitive fields automatically and recommends appropriate minimisation, masking, pseudonymisation, encryption and lawful basis considerations. Identifies data categories, lawful basis, retention, risks, mitigation controls and tags PII and special-category data while flagging cross-border restrictions (e.g., SAR segmentation).
column5:
- A single integrated modelling workflow reduces time, increases consistency and minimises redesign cycles
- Drastically accelerates modelling delivery, improves governance readiness and ensures alignment with BCDM, EDP, CDE/EDE and organisational modelling standards
- Reduces fragmentation, improves cross-domain interoperability and prevents downstream issues in lineage, DQ and transformations
- Privacy and PII detection built into modelling ensures regulatory compliance from day one
column8: Highly comprehensive use case that addresses a genuine pain point: data modelling is time-consuming, error-prone and governance-critical. Claude Code's ability to ingest heterogeneous inputs (Jira stories, legacy schemas, SME notes) and produce consistent, governance-ready outputs is well-suited. PII detection and BCDM alignment add significant compliance value.

column4: Claude automates the entire data design workflow by transforming raw discovery inputs (notes, Jira stories, meeting summaries, business requirements and legacy specifications) into complete, governance-ready Data Product Designs. Produces full functional and technical specifications including mappings, record structures, lineage, business rules, privacy requirements, controls, dependencies and usage notes. Generates comprehensive lineage across ingest → refine → curated layers by analysing SQL logic and transformation rules. Produces attribute-level lineage that meets governance, certification and Marketplace standards. Creates a full glossary and attribute dictionary including business definitions, technical semantics, permitted values, classifications and CDE/EDE linkage. Interprets sensitivity and architectural considerations to recommend end-to-end CI/CS measures (Confidentiality, Integrity, Cyber Security).
column5:
- Accelerates design creation, reducing hours or days of manual drafting into polished standardised documents
- Improves completeness and consistency across product documentation
- Automated lineage and metadata raise trust scores, boost Marketplace discoverability and improve certification outcomes
- Unified design workflow leads to faster delivery, higher-quality data products and more predictable enterprise governance cycles
column8: Valuable use case that builds directly on Data Modelling (#25) but focuses on the downstream design artefacts. The automation of specification documents, lineage and attribute dictionaries is a real productivity multiplier. Slightly derivative of the modelling use case — consider whether these should be presented as sub-items of a unified 'Data Architecture' use case.
